title: Self-test: Vol I, Ch 2: System Paradigms

questions.prompt: A safety-critical braking system has a 10 ms end-to-end budget and a cloud data center 1,500 km away. Light in fiber moves at $\approx 200{,}000$ km/s. Why is cloud offload physically impossible?

options.label: Cloud queue latency always adds $\ge 25$ ms regardless of load
The fiber round trip fits in 5 ms, but weight serialization takes 15 ms
Minimum propagation alone is 15 ms: the whole budget and more, before compute begins
Wireless protocols require a $\ge 50$ ms handshake first

questions.explanation: $2 \times 1500 / 200{,}000 = 0.015$ s $= 15$ ms of pure propagation, over the 10 ms budget before routing, queuing, or a single FLOP. Propagation is a floor, not a parameter.

questions.prompt: Which pairing matches workload archetype, dominant bottleneck, and lighthouse model?

options.label: Compute-bound → irregular table lookups and cache misses → DLRM
Bandwidth-bound → dense weight streaming in autoregressive decode → GPT-2/Llama
Capacity-bound → dense FLOP throughput at high arithmetic intensity → ResNet-50
Power-bound → petabyte distributed training → KWS

questions.explanation: Autoregressive decode streams the whole weight set per token with little reuse. (a) DLRM is capacity-bound; (c) ResNet-50 is compute-bound; (d) KWS is ~200 KB at ~1 mW, the opposite of petabyte training.

questions.prompt: Under dynamic CMOS scaling with $V \propto f$, doubling clock frequency raises dynamic power by a factor of 8.

options.label: True
False

questions.explanation: $P \propto C V^2 f$, $V \propto f$ gives $P \propto f^3$; $2^3 = 8$. This is the engine behind the power wall and the ~2005 clock freeze.

questions.prompt: When does the additive iron law apply versus the bottleneck max form?

options.label: Additive for one request's serialized latency; max for the steady-state completion interval of an overlapped stream
Additive for cloud workloads, max for TinyML
Additive above batch 128, max at batch 1
Additive in training, max in quantization

questions.explanation: The additive form prices one dependent path end to end. The max form prices the interval between completions of an overlapped stream: the slowest stage hides the rest, overhead sits outside the max.

questions.prompt: A drone at 60 fps (16.7 ms frame budget) captures uncompressed 4K frames (~24.9 MB) over a 100 Mbps uplink. Remote round trip plus inference is 110 ms. Applying the data locality invariant, cloud offload is:

options.label: Feasible: the cloud GPU infers in under 10 ms
Feasible with 5G network slicing enabled
Infeasible: drones cannot speak cloud telemetry protocols
Infeasible: transmission alone is ~2,000 ms, so even the lower bound (~2,100 ms) misses the deadline by two orders of magnitude

questions.explanation: $199.2$ Mbit $/ 100$ Mbps $\approx 1{,}992$ ms transmission alone; +110 ms remote ≈ 2.1 s vs 16.7 ms. 5G raises bandwidth, not propagation; the bound fails, so the path is rejected without measuring remote compute.

questions.prompt: How does the memory wall manifest given historical growth rates?

options.label: Bandwidth doubles every 18 months while compute grows 20%/yr
Both grow ~60%/yr but capacity limits model size
Thermal limits hit absolute while memory signaling energy is near zero
Compute doubles ~every 18 months (~60%/yr) while bandwidth grows ~20%/yr, so the gap compounds

questions.explanation: The ~1.6× vs ~1.2× annual divergence (ratio ≈ 1.33) is the memory wall: movement gains share of time and energy every generation.

questions.prompt: Explain to a junior dev why "the model is memory-bound" is an incomplete statement. What else must be specified for the claim to mean something?
questions.modelAnswer: The bound is a property of (workload × batch × precision × hardware), not the model. ResNet-50 is compute-bound at batch 256 and bandwidth-bound at batch 1. To say "memory-bound" you must name the machine's balance point ($R_{\mathrm{peak}}/BW$) and the workload's arithmetic intensity under those execution conditions.

questions.prompt: Why does the screening order put privacy before latency and cost last? What happens if you run the checks in the wrong order?
questions.modelAnswer: The order ranks how quickly a check can invalidate a candidate for free. A legal prohibition removes a tier before any number is computed; latency needs one lower bound; resources need device specs; cost is the only check that compares rather than rejects, so it belongs last, run only on survivors. Reordering wastes effort costing out paths that physics or law already killed.

questions.prompt: A colleague proposes fixing a phone's thermal throttling by quantizing the model to INT8. Explain why that helps the footprint and still fails the sustained workload.
questions.modelAnswer: INT8 quarters the footprint, which helps the capacity check and moves fewer bytes per inference. But sustained power is the binding term: switching energy and static leakage don't scale with weight precision, so a continuous pipeline above the ~2.5-5 W thermal envelope still throttles. The fix is a lower duty cycle, different silicon, or a different architecture.

questions.prompt: A warehouse camera records 1080p RGB frames (1920×1080×3 B ≈ 6.2 MB) at 30 fps for defect flagging over a 50 Mbps uplink. The per-frame deadline is one frame interval. (a) Transmission time per frame? (b) Does the remote path survive the locality screen, and if not, what is the cheapest fix that keeps cloud analytics?
questions.modelAnswer: (a) $6.2\text{ MB} \times 8 = 49.8$ Mbit $/ 50$ Mbps $\approx 996$ ms per frame. (b) The frame interval is $1/30$ s ≈ 33 ms, so transmission alone misses by ~30×: the remote path is rejected. Cheapest fix keeping cloud analytics: local flagging/filtering (send defect frames or crops only), the hierarchical pattern. Transmission drops ~100×+, and surviving frames fit easily inside the deadline.
